name.ja: 天ぷら まるや（デモ用サンプル店舗）

en.title: Tendon (tempura rice bowl)
en.extended_translation: Two shrimp and three seasonal vegetables, fried crisp and laid over hot rice, then glazed with a warm sweet-savory sauce. It was born in Edo-period Tokyo as fast food for working people — a complete meal in a single bowl, eaten quickly and with appetite.
en.scene_summary: The shop's signature bowl: shrimp and vegetable tempura over rice with tare sauce.

tags.title: Tendon
tags.description: Shrimp and seasonal vegetable tempura served over rice, finished with a soy-based sweet-savory sauce (tare) poured over the top.
tags.why_it_matters: It began as stand-up fast food for laborers in Edo-period Tokyo and is still a lunch staple today — everyday comfort food, not a special-occasion dish.

tags.title: Tare sauce
tags.description: A warm sauce of soy sauce, mirin and dashi. Each shop guards its own blend, some kept going for decades.
tags.why_it_matters: The sauce is what makes one shop's tendon taste different from another's — regulars often choose a shop by its tare.

en.cultural_gap: In Japan, a rice bowl topped with fried food is everyday comfort food. The crisp coating softening slightly in the sauce is part of the pleasure, not a flaw.
en.curiosity_hook: Which topping would you lift first — the shrimp, or a vegetable?

ja.title: 天丼
ja.extended_translation: 海老2本と季節野菜3種を揚げたてでのせ、温かい甘辛ダレを回しかけた一杯。江戸時代に働く人々の手早い食事として生まれ、丼ひとつで完結する東京の定番です。
ja.scene_summary: 看板商品。海老と野菜の天ぷらをご飯にのせ、タレをかけた丼。

tags.title: 天丼
tags.description: 海老と季節野菜の天ぷらをご飯にのせ、醤油ベースの甘辛いタレをかけたもの。
tags.why_it_matters: 江戸時代に労働者の立ち食いとして生まれ、今も昼食の定番。特別な料理ではなく日常の comfort food である。

tags.title: タレ
tags.description: 醤油・みりん・出汁を合わせた温かいタレ。配合は店ごとの秘伝で、継ぎ足して使い続ける店もある。
tags.why_it_matters: 天丼の味の決め手はタレであり、常連はタレで店を選ぶことも多い。

ja.cultural_gap: 日本では揚げ物をご飯にのせた丼は日常食。衣がタレで少ししんなりするのも味のうちとされる。
ja.curiosity_hook: 最初に食べたいのは海老ですか、野菜ですか？

en.title: Shrimp tempura set meal (teishoku)
en.extended_translation: Three shrimp and seasonal vegetables as tempura, served the teishoku way: on a tray with rice, miso soup and pickles, each in its own small dish. A teishoku is a complete, balanced meal built around one main dish — the standard shape of a Japanese lunch.
en.scene_summary: Shrimp tempura served as a full set meal with rice, miso soup and pickles.

tags.title: Teishoku (set meal)
tags.description: A tray set of a main dish, rice, miso soup and pickles. The idea is balance: a little of everything, arranged so the meal completes itself.
tags.why_it_matters: Teishoku is the default format of everyday eating out in Japan. Knowing the format tells you what will arrive before you order.

tags.title: How it is eaten
tags.description: There is no strict rule, but a common rhythm is a bite of tempura, a little rice, then a sip of miso soup — moving around the tray rather than finishing one dish at a time.
tags.why_it_matters: The rice is there to reset the palate between bites of fried food, which is why it is served plain.

en.cultural_gap: Outside Japan a 'set' often means a discount bundle. A teishoku is instead a composition: the soup and pickles are part of the dish, not extras.
en.curiosity_hook: Would you start with the shrimp, or save it for last?

ja.title: 海老天ぷら定食
ja.extended_translation: 海老3本と季節野菜の天ぷらを、ご飯・味噌汁・漬物と一緒に盆に揃えた定食形式。主菜を中心に食事全体が完結する、日本の昼食の標準形です。
ja.scene_summary: 海老天ぷらをご飯・味噌汁・漬物と揃えた定食。

tags.title: 定食
tags.description: 主菜・ご飯・味噌汁・漬物を一揃いにした形式。少しずつ多品目を揃え、食事として完結させる考え方。
tags.why_it_matters: 日本の外食の標準形であり、形式を知れば注文前に何が出るか分かる。

tags.title: 食べ方
tags.description: 厳密な決まりはないが、天ぷら一口、ご飯少し、味噌汁一口と、盆の上を回るように食べるのが一般的。
tags.why_it_matters: 白いご飯は揚げ物の合間に口を整える役割を持ち、そのため味付けされていない。

ja.cultural_gap: 海外では「セット」は割引の束として捉えられがちだが、定食は汁物と漬物まで含めた一つの構成である。
ja.curiosity_hook: 海老は最初に食べますか、最後に残しますか？

en.title: Kakiage-don (mixed fritter rice bowl)
en.literal_translation: Mixed shrimp and vegetable fritter rice bowl
en.extended_translation: Small shrimp and onion are mixed into batter and fried together as one golden disc — that disc is kakiage. Served over rice with a sweet-savory sauce. English has no single word for it, because the technique itself, frying mixed ingredients as one piece, is the dish.
en.scene_summary: A crisp mixed fritter of small shrimp and onion over rice with sauce.

tags.title: Kakiage
tags.description: Chopped ingredients mixed into batter and fried as a single round fritter. Born at Edo-period street stalls as a way to make small, inexpensive ingredients into a satisfying topping.
tags.why_it_matters: It turns scraps into the main event — a good example of the no-waste instinct in Japanese everyday cooking.

tags.title: The texture
tags.description: Crisp edges, tender center. Because the ingredients are mixed, every bite contains shrimp, onion and batter together rather than one ingredient at a time.
tags.why_it_matters: That mixed bite is exactly what a plain translation cannot convey — and what the dish is loved for.

en.cultural_gap: A fritter made of mixed leftovers might sound humble, but kakiage is a named specialty with devoted fans — humble ingredients, deliberate technique.
en.curiosity_hook: Listen for the crunch at the edge of the disc — that is the part cooks are judged by.

ja.title: かき揚げ丼
ja.extended_translation: 小海老と玉ねぎを衣に混ぜて一枚に揚げた「かき揚げ」を、ご飯にのせて甘辛ダレをかけた丼。具材を混ぜて一体に揚げる技法そのものが料理名になっており、英語に一語の対応がありません。
ja.scene_summary: 小海老と玉ねぎのかき揚げをご飯にのせた丼。

tags.title: かき揚げ
tags.description: 刻んだ具材を衣に混ぜ、一枚の円盤状に揚げた天ぷら。江戸の屋台で、小さく安い具材を満足感のある一品にするために生まれた。
tags.why_it_matters: 端材を主役に変える、日本の日常料理の「無駄にしない」発想の好例。

tags.title: 食感
tags.description: 縁はカリッと、中心はしっとり。具材が混ざっているため、一口ごとに海老・玉ねぎ・衣が一緒に来る。
tags.why_it_matters: この「混ざった一口」こそが直訳では伝わらず、この品が愛される理由である。

ja.cultural_gap: 混ぜ物の揚げ物は質素に聞こえるかもしれないが、かき揚げは名のある専門品であり、端材と技法の組み合わせが価値になっている。
ja.curiosity_hook: 円盤の縁のカリッという音に注目 — 職人の腕が一番出る部分です。
